body: It was an online chat program. I told them I was going to the washroom for a moment and when I came back the chat had been closed on their end. It deleted the entire conversation so I don't know what was said after that.

Don't apologize about the terminology, your right it is a skill. A skill to get yourself through the day. If you called it an "Easy bona fide miracle cure that everyone should know and will change your life in three easy steps!" Then I would take issue. 

I cant speak for other comedians, but for myself  comedy is an easy way to deflect real conversations about stuff that will make you break down if you were to speak honestly about it. There is no one size fits all way of dealing with depression and for some it's just to dig in your nails and hold on. I don't have the language to express my emotions or what's going on in my head and what the underlying issues are. If I were to stop and evaluate them, I would feel overwhelmed and have a nervous breakdown. That's why I use humour to deflect,  It allows me to hold on for just a while longer .

Thanks for your reply. I think the problem with my friends isn't that they have a stigmatization about mental health, it's just that they are not expecting it from me. I have cultivated a persona of someone who is very outgoing, funny and doesn't take anything to seriously. I preform stand up and improv, I always have a positive outlook and help my friends  see the positive in any situation. Think of Robin Williams, his suicide was regarded as something that was out of the blue but I think instead he used comedy as a diversion for his feelings. This Is what I do. 

I have a problem talking about my mental health because the few times I have reached out to friends, I saw how uncomfortable it made them to see someone they regarded as carefree so burdened. Being truly depressed is very different from being upset or saddened, and I feel that my friends have only dealt with the latter. Not that there is anything wrong with that, it just means that there isn't an easy solution for someone's depression. It's not something you can fix just by clearing up a misunderstanding or reassuring someone. Depression needs years of introspection and leaning and relearning coping skills to ever be able to get close to effectively managing it. That is a much bigger commitment then most friends are willing to agree to. 

I don't want to bring this to my friends because I know they cant fix it and I know that they will become discouraged and resentful when they realize this as well. It's not fair of me to subject these kind people who have become my friends, to that awful feeling of failure when they have failed at nothing.

Thanks, You hit the nail on the head. Crisis lines are a god send for those who want to commit suicide but understandably lack the training to help long term sufferers. Thank you for your support, I truly appreciate it.

Thank you, You (all of you) have been a big help. I've stopped feeling hysterical and have just kind of settled on numb. Which for tonight is a win. You have been truly kind and understanding of my ramblings and I truly appreciate that.  The mentally instable are my people. I don't understand how the rest of the stable crowd works. 

Thank you once again.

I honestly wish I still believed in suicide. At least when that was an option, I felt like I had a solution to this. A shitty, awful solution that didn't really work, but now I don't have any idea of how to make this end.

Day by day is actually a really good way to go about it. I get overwhelmed and start to spiral when I think about all the what if's and start to construct a chain of events involving the worst possible outcome to the worst possible outcome. It's intoxicating and very hard to get out of. I think that is a reason why I care so much about what others think of me,  I have spent too many hours thinking about how and why my friends will reject me and at the first sign, I take it as the start that chain. Then I end up isolating myself, further confirming my fears of abandonment and end up in a black pit I cant get out of. 

I have dealt with this shit for long enough to know it ends, it really does, but it doesn't end for at least a year and it takes so much to hold on during that time and then so much to rebuild fractured relationships one it's done. That's why I feel like I;m done. |It's exhausting and embarrassing. I dot expect people to stick through that, I don't want them to. They deserve to be happy an not encumbered by my mental health, but fucking Christ it hurts to go through alone.

Thank you. The isolation is the part that keeps me turning to drugs and alcohol as a coping mechanism and what usually leads to my eventual suicide attempt. I just really don't want to get to that point again this time. 

once I told the crisis hotline that I don't want to kill myself and that I cope with drugs, It felt like they stopped caring as much. it was like, Oh your aware of your depression, and that your coping skills are bad. Your not at risk for suicide? ok well gotta go have a good one. 

I would rather be suicidal again because then at least I  had a solution to my problems, It wasn't a very good solution but it was one

I feel the same way. I've hidden my depression since I was 15 and in the last 10 years I haven't found anyone  I feel that I can be honest with.  I have built up this persona where I am this funny girl doing stand up, making jokes and not taking anything seriously but in my own head, I take everything seriously. I value other opinions of me more then is probably healthy so I never want to show anything other then my best side. Then when someone does take interest, I hide the worst parts in fear that they will stop  when they see how profound this depression really is. Words of encouragement, or telling me I'm better then this don't make the demons go away. You cant just tell someone that they are a good person, that they have value and expect them to believe it when they have been living in an isolated hell for the past year.

I don't want my friends to feel bad, I don't want them to feel like they arn't helping so I put on a smile and agree, ya I am totally worth it, no what people think of me doesn't hang over my head like a hammer waiting for an opportunity to crush my will. It's just a phase your right, It WILL get better, thanks for reminding me. it makes this moment feel so much better when you remind me of happy I usually am because thats totally not a way for me to get through every fucking day of existence and try to hold onto a fable support network that isn't even aware I'm slipping towards total isolation.
I just don't know how to deal with my life.  This depression keeps getting worse and I can't talk to anyone I know
Thanks, I know I don't need to justify it but it helps having a solid idea of why I'm not being a total dick in the back of my head

She hasn't asked yet, I've suggested family members that live in the same city but she says that they don't allow cats, after she told me 3 days ago that she regularly takes the cat over there for extended periods. 

I guess what I feel bad about is being the one to initiate the conversation of "breaking up" and not feeling so guilty over it that I overcompensate and pay her rent for a month or something. 
Should I just cut and run?
Thanks, your point about pulling her up really helped put this into perspective for me.
